title: WPSS/1609/2014 of Smt Manju Giri Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1609 (S/S) of 2014
Smt. Manju Giri Ö.....Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö..Ö..Respondents
Mr. K.N. Joshi, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. T.P.S. Takuli, Brief Ho

lder, for the State.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)

1. Counter affidavit filed today in the Court by
respondent Nos. 2 and 4 is taken on record.
2. The petitioner before this Court was a candidate
for the post of Assistant Teacher in Government Primary
School for District Almora. She has admittedly all the
qualifications, including B.Ed. and Teacherís Eligibility Test
(in short ìTETî), which are minimum prescribed qualification
for the said post. The candidature of the petitioner was
considered, however, in the counseling the petitioner was
informed though the name of the petitioner was registered
with the Employment Exchange, but the same has not been
renewed, therefore, her candidature is rejected.
3. The admitted fact is that the petitioner was
registered with the Employment Office, Udham Singh Nagar
on 19.11.2007, which was valid upto 13.11.2010 and
thereafter she renewed the same upto November, 2013, but
thereafter, she did not renewed it in time, whereas the
renewal was only sought by her in the month of March, 2014
and the Employment Officer, Udham Singh Nagar issued her
fresh registration certificate to the petitioner on 25.03.2014.
4. In the counter affidavit the stand of the State
Government is that on the date of the relevant date the
petitioner was not registered with the Employment Exchange.
Though registration with the Employment Exchange is a
basic requirement, as per the Government Order placed

2
before this Court, but the fact that petitioner was registered
initially has not been denied. It was merely a lapse on the
part of the petitioner for not having renewed the registration,
which was subsequently done. Moreover, if for a certain
period, the name of the petitioner does not figure in the
Employment Exchange this itself cannot be a ground for
rejecting the claim of the petitioner. In any case the select
list was announced on 28.09.2014, and by that time the
petitioner was already registered with the Employment
Exchange.
5. Considering that her name was registered initially
with the Employment Exchange, at best the respondents,
who had noticed this irregularity in the candidature of the
petitioner could have given the petitioner appropriate time to
get itself registered with the Employment Exchange. This has
not been done in the present case. Therefore, non-consideration of the petitioner case for appointment seems to
be arbitrary.
6. In view of the above, the writ petition is allowed.
The impugned order dated 18.10.2014 passed by respondent
No. 4 is hereby quashed.
7. A mandamus is hereby issued to the respondent to
appoint the petitioner forthwith on the post of Assistant
Teacher in Government Primary School, unless there is some
other ineligibility attached to the petitioner.
8. Let the needful be done as expeditiously as
possible, but definitely within a period of six weeks from the
date of production of certified copy of this order.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 18.11.2014
Nitesh
